* Toronto stocks were expected to continue their rise at the open on Thursday in the absence of rate hike fears. * Analysts said banks would drive the market higher.
Toronto stocks were expected to continue their rise on Thursday amid receding rate hike fears, with analysts saying the market could break through its all-time high in the near term.

"We're out of the interest rate anxiety right now. That will creep up again in the first week of July...I can see the Canadian market going through that all-time high, on into 64, 6500, by the summer," said Ira Katzin, investment adviser at RBC Dominion Securities.
He said Canadian investors would likely move into high quality stocks as economic growth slowed in the medium term.
"I think that the economic numbers are pointing toward growth at diminishing rates over the next couple of quarters and I think that's what's going to guide investors," Katzin said.
He said bank issues should continue to lead the market as the sector benefited from diminished interest rate hike fears.
"We're looking for better performances, continuation of the rising trend of the bank issues, primarily because of their quality, predictability of earnings, (and) rising dividends," he said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished 47 points higher on Wednesday at 6307.13, close to its record high of 6348.02 points set on March 11.
U.S. treasuries were modestly lower in early trade after U.S. jobless claims data came in slightly below expectations.
In Canadian economic news, the composite leading indicator rose 0.8 percent in April to 192.2 (base 1981) after a 0.9 percent rise in March.
Foreign investors sold a net C$2.144 billion in Canadian securities in March, after buying a net C$1.28 billion in February (revised from C$1.13 billion).
